prompt: Why are ethers generally UNREACTIVE in the lab compared to alcohols?

options.label: No acidic O-H bond, strong C-O bond, and OR⁻ is a poor leaving group
Ethers are essentially nonpolar — no dipole for nucleophiles to grip
The lone pairs on O are symmetrically placed, canceling their nucleophilicity
The ether O's lone pairs are tied up in σ hyperconjugation with adjacent C-H bonds

explanation: Ethers lack the acidic O-H of alcohols AND lack a good leaving group (OR⁻ is terrible — pKa of ROH ~16). They're used as solvents (Et₂O, THF, dioxane) precisely BECAUSE they're inert — they just H-bond accept. Only strong acids (HI, HBr), epoxides' ring strain, or peroxide chemistry disrupt them.
